title: Barista App Manifest
description: Portable, least-privilege declaration for packaging and running a Barista application on any conformant Host API provider. Media type: application/vnd.barista.app-manifest.v1alpha1+json

schema_version.description: Manifest schema version. Establishes wire compatibility.

name.description: App name. Reverse-DNS or short identifier; combined with version and workload digest it is the app identity.

version.description: App version (semver recommended). Part of app identity together with the workload digest.

endpoints.description: Optional service endpoints the workload exposes.

metadata.description: Opaque, namespaced app metadata. A host preserves recognized envelope constraints without understanding any specific harness. Keys are app namespaces (reverse-DNS).

oci_digest.description: Immutable OCI content digest, e.g. sha256:<64 hex>.

image.description: OCI image reference. A mutable tag here is a human label only and does NOT establish app identity.

digest.description: Immutable image digest. Establishes executable identity. Required.

entrypoint.description: Command executed to start the workload.

readiness.description: How the host determines the workload is ready to serve.

command.description: For type=exec: command whose zero exit means ready.

http_path.description: For type=http: path polled for a 2xx.

log_pattern.description: For type=log_line: regex matched against stdout/stderr.

capability_id.description: A discoverable Host API capability/profile identifier.

constraints.description: Optional semantic constraints (e.g. min limits) the provider must satisfy.

capabilities.description: Host capabilities the app needs. Required capabilities must be advertised by the provider before any side effect; the discovered optional set is delivered to the app at launch.

action_id.description: A Host API action the app may perform. Least-privilege.

action_scope.description: WHICH sessions a declared action may target, relative to the session that holds the authority. 'own_session': only the session the grant was minted for. 'created_sessions': only the sessions that session itself created — never a sibling, a parent, or any other session in the account. A provider SHALL NOT widen a declared scope.

action_grant.description: One declared action together with the sessions it applies to. Two equivalent forms: a bare action id, which means exactly {"action": <id>, "scope": "own_session"} and is kept for manifests written before scopes existed; or the object form, which states the scope at the point of declaration. The same action MAY appear once per scope. 'session.create' is collection-level — it authorizes creating a child session and is bounded by permissions.child_sessions, not by a scope — so it is declared as a bare action id and the object form rejects it.

not.description: session.create takes no scope; declare it as the bare action id.

permissions.description: Least-privilege declaration of what the app is allowed to do. Contains only secret references, never plaintext.

actions.description: Actions the app itself may perform, each with the sessions it applies to. See $defs/action_grant: a bare action id means the app's own session only; the object form states the scope explicitly.

secrets.description: Secret references by name only. Plaintext is rejected.

publication.description: Publication surfaces the app may use (e.g. story).

degraded_modes.description: Named degraded modes the app can validly run in when a host grants less than requested.

allow.description: For egress=allowlist: host or host:port entries.

ref.description: Provider-resolvable reference (a scheme URI such as secret://, grant://, ref://, vault://, or env://). NEVER a plaintext value — the pattern rejects a bare credential.

child_session_limits.description: Bounds AND authority for the sessions this app creates. The counts bound HOW MANY children; 'actions' declares WHAT a child receives; 'allow_descendants' declares whether a child may create sessions of its own. A block carrying only the counts — every manifest written before those two fields existed — means a child receives no delegated authority at all, which is unchanged behaviour.

actions.description: The actions a child session receives. The provider is the only minter: it mints this set as the child's grant at child-session create; the parent never handles that credential. Scopes here are relative to the CHILD ('own_session' = the child itself, 'created_sessions' = the grandchildren the child creates). This set MUST be a subset of the app's own — a rule JSON Schema CANNOT express and therefore does NOT enforce. See contracts/app-manifest/README.md ('The subset rule') and the reference implementation in rules.py.

allow_descendants.description: Whether a child session may itself create further sessions. Absent or false: it may not, even though the app itself may — the ratified factory-app scenario. When it is not true, 'actions' MUST NOT contain session.create; the schema enforces that much.

state_transfer.description: Hooks for exact (capsule) and semantic (adapter) session transfer.

exact.description: Whether this app's sessions can be exactly forked/captured (requires provider capability).

adapter.description: Adapter namespace responsible for semantic export/continuation (e.g. sh.barista.adapter.pi).
